history.period: 10th century CE - built by Raja Sahil Varman (Sahil Verman), founder of Chamba town, c. 920 CE
history.summary: The Lakshmi Narayan temple group is the main and oldest surviving Vaishnavite shrine complex of Chamba town, Himachal Pradesh: six shikhara-style temples running north to south. The main Lakshmi Narayan temple was built in the 10th century CE by Raja Sahil Varman, the founder of Chamba (c. 920 AD) - CORRECTION: the CSV detail hint says '10th c. Meru Varman', but Meru Varman ruled in the 7th century (and built the Lakshana Devi temple at Bharmaur); Sahil Varman is the builder attested by all consulted sources. The main shrine has a bimana (shikhara), garbhagriha with small antarala and mandapa, wooden chhatris and a wheel-shaped shell roof against snowfall, with a white marble Vishnu murti (stone said to have been brought from the Vindhyas) and a brass Garuda at the entrance. The complex also holds the Lakshmi-Damodar temple (three-headed Vishnu), Gauri Shankar (built by Sahil Varman's son Yugkar Varman), the Chandragupta Shiva temple (built by Sahil Varman), and the Radha Krishna temple (built by Rani Sarda in 1825). Located in Chowgan Mohalla, about 200 m from the Chaugan. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name ('Chamba') - the real state is HIMACHAL PRADESH.

name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple
town_description: Chamba is the old princely-capital town of Chamba district, Himachal Pradesh, set on a plateau on the right bank of the Ravi at about 996 m, surrounded by the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges. Founded c. 920 CE by Raja Sahil Varman, it is one of the oldest continuously inhabited towns in the western Himalaya, known for its ancient temple cluster around the Chaugan (town green), Chamba rumal embroidery, and the Minjar and Sui Mata festivals.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavite, with Shaivite shrines in the same complex)
